acceptance.output_evidence: The reading is delivered in three parts in section 6 of the record and is NOT self-graded. (a) THE REMEDY: the right remedy IS upstream and the drop is still the correct thing to ship. The disease is that the producer's INPUT contains its own OUTPUT (derive_runner folds the artifact into the snapshot it archives, derive_stitch reads that snapshot back); every carrier-level fix is a filter compensating for an input that should not contain the producer's own claims -- three filters now, each correct, none able to say anything about a fourth carrier. The upstream remedy is one filter at ONE place (the fold writes stitch members to a separate document, or load_aws_layer strips source=portal-stitch at the door), and it is derive_runner's surface, i.e. the NEXT order's, so this order does not take it. The drop is right BECAUSE the door is open: with it open, a node this cycle did not emit is stale data being served tonight, and no upstream elegance retro-fixes tonight's artifact. (b) A FOURTH CARRIER, BY CONSTRUCTION AND NOT BY A FOURTH CHECK -- the third check is the evidence that checks do not generalise. Three things, none a monitor: (i) a CYCLE STAMP on every emitted member, because source=portal-stitch says WHO and never WHEN, which is why the producer had to reach for python id() -- an in-process identity standing in for a freshness field the DATA does not carry, reproducible by no consumer and no later reader; (ii) ONE prior-cycle filter AT THE READ, applied to the whole document before any carrier-specific logic sees it, so a new carrier inherits the answer instead of being asked the question again; (iii) a reconciliation that counts INPUTS -- the producer's 'admitted = merged + created, lost = 0' is a conservation law over what it ADMITTED and is structurally incapable of noticing that its input held 1,771 members it never derived. The tell in any future producer: a conservation law whose denominator is the producer's own output. (c) WAS THE DIFFERENCE DEFENSIBLE? In sequence, yes; at rest, no. Each rule was a correct local repair under a different pressure (a vocabulary change, a retired stamp, a 955-edge fan-out) by a seat that could see one carrier. What was never defensible is the STATE it left: one mechanism, three answers, no document saying they answered the same question, and a per-carrier check that passes on each. The narrow rule worth keeping: WHEN A PRODUCER READS ITS OWN OUTPUT, THE ANSWER TO 'IS THE PRIOR CYCLE INPUT OR NOISE?' IS A PROPERTY OF THE PRODUCER AND MUST BE WRITTEN ONCE, AT THE READ -- if it is being answered at the carrier, that is already the defect, and the number of carriers is just how many times you will find it.
